1. [TEMPORAL] The DV-2024 entry period will run from 12:00 pm (noon), Eastern Daylight Time (EDT) on Wednesday, October 5, 2022, until 12:00 pm (noon), Eastern Standard Time (EST) on Tuesday, November 8, 2022.
2. [FACT] Each year, millions of people submit entries for the DV program.
3. [ASSISTANT_SAID] Restricting the entry period to these dates ensures selectees receive notification in a timely manner and gives both the visa applicants and embassies and consulates time to prepare and complete cases for visa issuance.
4. [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is strongly encouraged to enter early during the registration period to avoid excessive demand that may slow the processing system.
5. [FACT] Entries cannot be accepted after noon EST on Tuesday, November 8, 2022.
6. [FACT] An entrant may apply while in the United States or another country.
7. [FACT] An entrant may submit an entry from any location.
8. [FACT] The law allows only one entry per person during each registration period.
9. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Department of State uses sophisticated technology to detect multiple entries, and individuals with more than one entry will be ineligible for a DV.
10. [FACT] Each spouse may submit one entry if each meets the eligibility requirements.
11. [ASSISTANT_SAID] If either spouse is selected, the other is entitled to apply as a derivative dependent.
12. [FACT] If legally married, you must list your spouse regardless of whether he/she lives with you or intends to immigrate to the United States.
13. [ASSISTANT_SAID] You must list your spouse even if you are currently separated unless you are legally separated by court order.
14. [FACT] Legal separation is an arrangement when a couple remains married but lives apart, following a court order.
15. [ASSISTANT_SAID] If you and your spouse are legally separated, your spouse will not be able to immigrate with you through the Diversity Visa program.
16. [FACT] You will not be penalized if you choose to enter the name of a spouse from whom you are legally separated.
17. [FACT] If you are not legally separated by a court order, you must include your spouse even if you plan to be divorced before applying for the Diversity Visa.
18. [FACT] You do not have to list your former spouse if you are divorced or your spouse is deceased.
19. [ASSISTANT_SAID] Parents and siblings of the entrant are ineligible to receive DV visas
